rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meet their harm with patience and forgiveness; this command preceded fighting.
rows.anchor: { ادفع بالتي هي أحسن } من الحلم والصفح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan's incitements and whispers are the objects of the Prophet's refuge-seeking.
rows.anchor: { وقل رب أعوذ بك من همزات الشياطين } نزغاتها ووساوسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also seeks refuge from Satan's presence in any of his affairs.
rows.anchor: { وأعوذ بك رب أن يحضرون } في شيء من أموري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When death comes, the person asks God to return him to worldly life.
rows.anchor: { رب ارجعون } أي: ارددني إلى الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hoped-for good deed is bearing witness to divine unity; God refuses the request, and a barrier blocks return to the world until resurrection.
rows.anchor: { لعلي أعمل صالحا } أي: أشهد بالتوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Barzakh means a barrier between the dead and return to worldly life.
rows.anchor: { ومن ورائهم } أمامهم { برزخ } حاجز بينهم وبين الرجوع إلى الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the final trumpet blast, people will not boast about lineage or ask about one another's tribe and ancestry as they did in worldly life.
rows.anchor: { فإذا نفخ في الصور } النفخة الأخيرة { فلا أنساب بينهم يومئذ } لا يفتخرون بالأنساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The damned mocked the believers until their mockery distracted them from remembering God.
rows.anchor: { فاتخذتموهم سخريا } أي: سخرتم منهم، واستهزأتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rewarded the believers for enduring abuse, making them the saved ones.
rows.anchor: { بما صبروا } على أذاكم { أنهم هم الفائزون } الناجون من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After raising deniers of resurrection from their graves, God asks how many years they remained there as a rebuke.
rows.anchor: { قال كم لبثتم في الأرض عدد سنين } قال الله تعالى لمنكري البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say a day or part of a day because punishment was lifted between the two blasts and they forgot their suffering.
rows.anchor: { قالوا لبثنا يوما أو بعض يوم } وذلك أن العذاب رفع عنهم فيما بين النفختين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They tell the questioner to ask the angels who counted their time.
rows.anchor: لبثنا يوما أو بعض يوم فاسأل العادين } أي: فاسأل الملائكة الذين يحفظون عدد ما لبثنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if the stay in Hell was long, it is little by comparison; knowing their grave-time would have shown it to be short beside their stay in the Fire.
rows.anchor: { قال إن لبثتم } ما لبثتم { إلا قليلا } وإن طال لبثكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People were not created pointlessly: there is a purpose of reward for the obedient and punishment for the disobedient.
rows.anchor: { أفحسبتم أنما خلقناكم عبثا } أي: للعبث لا لحكمة من ثواب للمطيع

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative gloss says they were created for play so that they might play, neglect, and amuse themselves.
rows.anchor: وقيل: عبثا للعبث، حتى تعبثوا وتغفلوا وتلهوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Noble Throne is glossed as a beautiful couch.
rows.anchor: { رب العرش الكريم } أي: السرير الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One who invokes another deity has no proof for doing so; God will reckon and repay him, and disbelievers do not prosper.
rows.anchor: { ومن يدع مع الله إلها آخر لا برهان له به } لا حجة له بما يفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God drives clouds where He wills, joins their pieces and stacks them; rain emerges through their gaps, while hail descends from mountains in the sky, striking some and sparing others, and lightning nearly blinds.
rows.anchor: { ألم تر أن الله يزجي } يسوق { سحابا } إلى حيث يريد { ثم يؤلف بينه } يجمع بين قطع ذلك السحاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The changing alternation of night and day is a lesson for people of understanding.
rows.anchor: { يقلب الله الليل والنهار } يصرفهما في اختلافهما وتعاقبهما { إن في ذلك } الذي ذكرت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every creature was made from water, glossed as a drop of fluid; some crawl on their bellies, some walk on two legs, and some on four.
rows.anchor: { والله خلق كل دابة من ماء } أي: من نطفة { فمنهم من يمشي على بطنه } كالحيات والحيتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The celestial mansions are stations of the seven planets, and the lamp is the sun.
rows.anchor: { تبارك الذي جعل في السماء بروجا } أي: منازل الكواكب السبعة { وجعل فيها سراجا } وهو الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night and day replace one another, so missed night worship can be made up in daytime; remembrance includes prayer, glorification, and recitation, and gratitude means thanking and obeying God.
rows.anchor: { وهو الذي جعل الليل والنهار خلفة } إذا ذهب هذا أتى هذا، فأحدهما يخلف الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servants of the All-Merciful are His chosen servants; they walk calmly and answer ignorant people with words that keep them from sin.
rows.anchor: { وعباد الرحمن } يعني: خواص عباده { الذين يمشون على الأرض هونا } بالسكينة والوقار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Winds herald rain and let people taste God's mercy; they also drive ships and enable trade at sea.
rows.anchor: { ومن آياته أن يرسل الرياح مبشرات } بالمطر { وليذيقكم من رحمته } نعمته بالمطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God punished the polytheist criminals and promised to grant believers victory in the end, including the Prophet over his opponents.
rows.anchor: { فانتقمنا من الذين أجرموا } أي: عاقبنا الذين اشركوا { وكان حقا علينا نصر المؤمنين } في العاقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God stirs clouds from their places, spreads them or divides them into pieces, and rain emerges from their middle and cracks; those who receive it rejoice.
rows.anchor: { الله الذي يرسل الرياح فتثير سحابا } تزعجها وتخرجها من أماكنها { فيبسطه } الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated phrase “before it” is for emphasis; before the rain comes they are despairing.
rows.anchor: { وإن كانوا من قبل أن ينزل عليهم } المطر { من قبله } كرر " من قبل " للتأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The initial human weakness from which God creates people is the drop of semen.
rows.anchor: { الله الذي خلقكم من ضعف } من نطفة. الآية.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At resurrection the disbelievers swear they remained in their graves less than an hour, continuing their worldly habit of lying.
rows.anchor: { ويوم تقوم الساعة يقسم المجرمون } يحلف الكافرون { ما لبثوا } في قبورهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those given knowledge and faith say the people remained, as God's Book states, until the Resurrection Day, which the deniers did not know would come.
rows.anchor: { وقال الذين أوتوا العلم والإيمان لقد لبثتم في كتاب الله } أي: فيما بين في كتابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guilty will not be asked to return to what pleases God.
rows.anchor: { ولا هم يستعتبون } أي: لا يطلب منهم أن يرجعوا إلى ما يرضي الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives parables for reflection, but even a clear sign would prompt disbelievers to call the messengers liars.
rows.anchor: { ولقد ضربنا للناس في هذا القرآن من كل مثل } بينا لهم الأمثال للاعتبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sorrow removed from the people of Paradise includes all worldly and otherworldly grief.
rows.anchor: { الحمد لله الذي أذهب عنا الحزن } يعني: كل ما يحزن له الإنسان من أمر المعاش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their eternal home is a gift of God's grace rather than their deeds, and it has neither fatigue nor exhaustion.
rows.anchor: { الذي أحلنا } أنزلنا { دار المقامة } دار الخلود { من فضله } أي: ذلك بتفضله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers remain in Hell without being put to death and released.
rows.anchor: { والذين كفروا لهم نار جهنم لا يقضى عليهم فيموتوا }.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They cry for help; the warned lifetime is one in which a person can take heed, identified here as sixty years.
rows.anchor: { وهم يصطرخون } يستغيثون. وقوله: { أولم نعمركم ما يتذكر فيه من تذكر }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation identifies the warner as the Messenger.
rows.anchor: { وجاءكم النذير } يعني: الرسول،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation identifies the warner as gray hair.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الشيب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the people successors on earth, meaning a community that came after earlier nations.
rows.anchor: { هو الذي جعلكم خلائف في الأرض } أي: جعلكم أمة خلقت من قبلها من الأمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge asks what the alleged partners created on earth or whether they share in creating heaven; the polytheists have no scripture proving their claim, and their mutual promises are delusions.
rows.anchor: { ماذا خلقوا من الأرض }. أي: بأي شيء أوجبتم لهم الشركة مع الله، ألخلق خلقوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God keeps the heavens and earth from moving away; if they moved, no one else could hold them.
rows.anchor: { إن الله يمسك السموات والأرض أن تزولا } لئلا تزولا وتتحركا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before Muhammad's mission the polytheists swore they would be more rightly guided than Jews, Christians, or Magians, but the Prophet's coming only increased their recoil from truth.
rows.anchor: { وأقسموا بالله جهد إيمانهم } يعني: المشركين، كانوا يقولون قبل بعثه محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God could blind them; then they could not see the path toward which they hurried.
rows.anchor: { ولو نشاء لطمسنا على أعينهم } لأعميناهم وأذهبنا أبصارهم { فاستبقوا الصراط }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God could transform them into stones, apes, or pigs in their homes, leaving them unable to go or return.
rows.anchor: { ولو نشاء لمسخناهم } حجارة وقردة وخنازير { على مكانتهم } في منازلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Long life reverses a person's condition: strength becomes weakness and youth becomes old age.
rows.anchor: { ومن نعمره ننكسه في الخلق } من أطلنا عمره نكسنا خلقه، فصار بدل القوة صعفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God did not teach Muhammad poetry, nor is it easy for him; what he brought is only a reminder and clear Qur'an.
rows.anchor: { وما علمناه الشعر } لم نعلم محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم قول الشعر { وما ينبغي له }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder warns the intellectually living, since the disbeliever is like the dead, and establishes the case against disbelievers.
rows.anchor: { لينذر من كان حيا } عاقلا، فلا يغفل ما يخاطب به؛ لأن الكافر كالميت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The losers lose themselves through everlasting residence in Hell and lose their families because they do not join believers' families in Paradise.
rows.anchor: { قل إن الخاسرين الذين خسروا أنفسهم } بالتخليد في النار { وأهليهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shade over the damned matches other descriptions of punishment above and below; God uses this punishment to warn His servants.
rows.anchor: { لهم من فوقهم ظلل } هذا كقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Taghut they avoid worshipping means idols; those who turn back to God do so through obedience and receive good news of Paradise.
rows.anchor: { والذين اجتنبوا الطاغوت } أي: الأوثان { أن يعبدوها وأنابوا إلى الله }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who listen to speech and follow its best part follow the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: { الذين يستمعون القول } القرآن وغيره { فيتبعون أحسنه } وهو القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad cannot rescue a person already sentenced to punishment by taking him out of the Fire.
rows.anchor: { أفمن حق عليه كلمة العذاب أفأنت } يا محمد { تنقذ } ه، أي: تخرجه من النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers receive high dwellings in Paradise, with even higher ones above them.
rows.anchor: { لهم غرف من فوقها غرف مبنية } أي: لهم منازل في الجنة رفيعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad should be patient because God's promise to aid him and destroy his enemies is true; glorifying with praise means praying gratefully at both ends of the day.
rows.anchor: { فاصبر } يا محمد { إن وعد الله } في نصرتك وإهلاك أعدائك { حق وسبح بحمد ربك }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opponents' inward arrogance and ambition to prevail over Muhammad will fail, so he should seek God's protection from them.
rows.anchor: { إن في صدورهم إلا كبر ما هم ببالغيه } أي: تكبر وطمع أن يعلوا على محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creating the heavens and earth displays greater power than recreating people for resurrection.
rows.anchor: { لخلق السموات والأرض أكبر من خلق الناس } أي: أعظم في القدرة من إعادة الناس للبعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Respond to God with faith and obedience before the irreversible Day; then there will be no escape from punishment and no ability to deny or change what befalls you.
rows.anchor: { استجيبوا لربكم } بالإيمان والطاعة { من قبل أن يأتي يوم لا مرد له من الله }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person who makes desire his religion follows anything he desires; God lets him stray according to prior knowledge of his misguidance.
rows.anchor: { أفرأيت من اتخذ إله هواه } أي: الكافر اتخذ دينه ما يهواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers claim this world is the only life: people die and their children live, and only the passage of time destroys them; they have no knowledge and merely conjecture.
rows.anchor: { وقالوا } يعني: منكري البعث: { ما هي إلا حياتنا الدنيا } أي: ما الحياة إلا هذه الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When shown clear proofs of God's power to resurrect, their only argument is to demand that their forefathers be brought back.
rows.anchor: { وما كان حجتهم إلا أن قالوا ائتوا بآبائنا إن كنتم صادقين } أنا نبعث بعد الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All messengers had resolve except Jonah; another view restricts the resolute messengers to the law-bearing Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad.
rows.anchor: { فاصبر كما صبر أولو العزم من الرسل } أي: ذوو الرأي والجد، وكلهم أولو العزم إلا يونس. وقيل: هم أصحاب الشرائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers will experience their worldly lifetime as only an hour of a day from the terror they witness and forget its length; this Qur'an is God's message, and only the disobedient perish.
rows.anchor: { كأنهم يوم يرون ما يوعدون } من العذاب في الآخرة { لم يلبثوا } في الدنيا { إلا ساعة من نهار }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Glorification before sunrise means the dawn prayer; before sunset means noon and afternoon prayers.
rows.anchor: { قبل طلوع الشمس } أي: صلاة الفجر { وقبل الغروب } صلاة الظهر والعصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night prayer means the two evening prayers, and glorification after prostrations means the two cycles after sunset prayer.
rows.anchor: { ومن الليل فسبحه } أي: صلاتي العشاء { وأدبار السجود } أي: الركعتين بعد المغرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The caller is Israfil, summoning decayed bones and scattered flesh to gather for judgment; he calls from the rock of Jerusalem, the nearest place on earth to heaven.
rows.anchor: { يوم ينادي المنادي } وهو إسرافيل عليه السلام يقول: أيتها العظام البالية، واللحوم المتمزقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The truthful cry is the blast of resurrection, marking emergence from graves.
rows.anchor: { يوم يسمعون الصيحة بالحق } أي: نفخة البعث { ذلك يوم الخروج } من القبور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire people kindle comes from a tree God created, not from them.
rows.anchor: { أأنتم أنشأتم } خلقتم { شجرتها } التي تخرج منها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire reminds people of Hell and benefits travelers.
rows.anchor: { نحن جعلناها تذكرة } يتذكر بها نار جهنم { ومتاعا } ومنفعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to glorify God declares Him far above what polytheists say.
rows.anchor: { فسبح باسم ربك العظيم } أي: نزه الله مما يقول المشركون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The negating particle in the oath is extra; the “settings of the stars” are their setting places and western horizons.
rows.anchor: { فلا أقسم } " لا " زائدة { بمواقع النجوم } مساقطها ومغاربها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the stars in the oath to mean the stars of the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أراد نجوم القرآن.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “witnesses” are prophets, who have their reward and light in the grave; another view says all believers are intended.
rows.anchor: { والشهداء عند ربهم } أي: الأنبياء عليهم السلام { لهم أجرهم ونورهم } في ظلمة القبر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative interpretation takes the witnesses to be all believers.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هم جميع المؤمنين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly life is passing play, diversion, adornment, boasting, and competition in wealth and children. Like rain-grown crops that yellow, dry, and crumble, people age, die, and decay; the afterlife holds punishment for disbelievers and forgiveness and approval for God's friends. Here “the disbelievers” means farmers.
rows.anchor: { اعلموا أنما الحياة الدنيا لعب ولهو } في انقضائها وقلة حاصلها { وزينة } يتزينون بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists' heedlessness resembles earlier disbelievers, identified as the people of Badr, who tasted punishment shortly before Banū al-Naḍīr were exiled after the Prophet returned from Uḥud.
rows.anchor: { كمثل الذين من قبلهم } أي: المشركين، يقول: هم في تركهم الإيمان وغفلتهم عن عذاب الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites' promised support and later abandonment of Banū al-Naḍīr resembles Satan tempting and then abandoning a worshipper among the Children of Israel.
rows.anchor: { كمثل الشيطان } يعني: إن المنافقين في نصرتهم لليهود كمثل الشيطان { إذ قال للإنسان اكفر }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan and the person he misled end up together in Hell forever, the punishment for wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: { فكان عاقبتهما } عاقبة الشيطان والكافر { أنهما في النار خالدين فيها وذلك جزاء الظالمين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should fulfill obligations, avoid sins, and consider the righteous deeds sent ahead for Resurrection Day.
rows.anchor: { يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله } بأداء فرائضه واجتناب معاصيه { ولتنظر نفس ما قدمت لغد }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wealth and children must not distract from God's remembrance, meaning the five daily prayers; those distracted from prayer are losers.
rows.anchor: { يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تلهكم } لا تشغلكم { أموالكم ولا أولادكم عن ذكر الله }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spending means paying zakat before death prompts a request for delay to give charity and become righteous, here glossed as performing pilgrimage; anyone falling short in zakat or pilgrimage asks to return at death.
rows.anchor: { وأنفقوا مما رزقناكم } يعني: أدوا الزكاة { من قبل أن يأتي أحدكم الموت فيقول: رب لولا أخرتني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will not delay a soul once its appointed time comes.
rows.anchor: { ولن يؤخر الله نفسا إذا جاء أجلها والله خبير بما تعملون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day of Mutual Loss shows the loss of disbelievers who forfeit the Paradise places they would have had if they believed, and of believers whose lesser rank reveals their shortcomings.
rows.anchor: { يوم التغابن } يغبن فيه أهل الجنة أهل النار بأخذ منازلهم التي كانت لهم في الجنة لو آمنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People with means must provide for their nursing wives according to their means; someone whose resources are only subsistence spends accordingly.
rows.anchor: { لينفق ذو سعة من سعته } أمر أهل التوسعة أن يوسعوا على نسائهم المرضعات أولادهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not overburden a person beyond what He gave; despite their poverty, believers would receive ease and expanded provision after hardship, as happened later.
rows.anchor: { لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا ما آتاها } أعطاها. { سيجعل الله بعد عسر يسرا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Defiant towns faced severe reckoning and dreadful punishment in the Fire; they tasted the heavy consequence of their conduct, ending in loss and ruin.
rows.anchor: { وكأين } وكم { من قرية عتت عن أمر ربها ورسله } عتا أهلها عما أمر الله تعالى به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tested Mecca's people with drought and famine as He tested orchard owners in Yemen by burning their garden. Their father used to feed the poor from it; after he died, his sons feared giving would leave them short, so they planned to harvest before the poor came.
rows.anchor: { إنا بلوناهم } امتحنا أهل مكة بالقحط والجوع { كما بلونا أصحاب الجنة } كما امتحنا أصحاب البستان بإحراقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They did not make an exception by saying “if God wills.”
rows.anchor: { ولا يستثنون } ولا يقولون إن شاء الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent a fire over the orchard while its owners slept and burned it.
rows.anchor: { فطاف عليها طائف من ربك وهم نائمون } أي: أنزل الله عليها نارا أحرقتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The orchard became black like a dark night.
rows.anchor: { فأصبحت كالصريم } كالليل المظلم سوداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At daybreak the brothers called one another to go harvest the fruit.
rows.anchor: { فتنادوا مصبحين } نادى بعضهم بعضا لما أصبحوا ليخرجوا إلى الصرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They urge one another to go to the crop and cut its fruit.
rows.anchor: { أن اغدوا على حرثكم إن كنتم صارمين } قاطعين الثمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They set out while whispering secretly among themselves.
rows.anchor: { فانطلقوا } ذهبوا إليها { وهم يتخافتون } يتسارون الكلام بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They conspire that no poor person should enter their orchard that day.
rows.anchor: { أن لا يدخلنها اليوم عليكم مسكين }.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They went with firm purpose, believing they had power over the garden's fruit.
rows.anchor: { وغدوا على حرد } قصد وجد { قادرين } عند أنفسهم على ثمر الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing it black and burned, they first thought they had lost their way, then realized God had deprived them of their fruit because they withheld it from the poor.
rows.anchor: { فلما رأوها } سوداء محترقة { قالوا إنا لضالون } مخطئون طريقنا، وليست هذه جنتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most balanced brother had asked them to glorify God, meaning to say “if God wills”; that exception counts as glorification because it exalts God.
rows.anchor: { قال أوسطهم } أعدلهم وأفضلهم: { ألم أقل لكم لولا تسبحون } هلا تستثنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They declare God free of wrongdoing and admit they wronged themselves.
rows.anchor: { قالوا سبحان ربنا } نزهوه عن أن يكون ظالما، وأقروا على أنفسهم بالظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They blame each other for fleeing the poor and withholding their due, confessing that they transgressed.
rows.anchor: { فأقبل بعضهم على بعض يتلاومون } يلوم بعضهم بعضا بما فعلوا من الهرب من المساكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They hope God will replace their orchard with a better one and turn to Him.
rows.anchor: { عسى ربنا أن يبدلنا خيرا منها } من هذه الجنة { إنا إلى ربنا راغبون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will punish those who disobey as He punished the orchard owners, while the God-fearing have gardens of bliss; some Quraysh retorted that if this were true, they would have more in the afterlife, prompting the following revelation.
rows.anchor: { كذلك العذاب } كما فعلنا بهم نفعل بمن خالف أمرنا، ثم بين ما عند الله للمؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person cannot ransom himself with everything on earth; nothing will save him, and Laẓā is a name of Hell.
rows.anchor: { ومن في الأرض جميعا ثم ينجيه } ذلك الافتداء. { كلا } ليس الأمر كذلك، لا ينجيه شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “It strips the scalp” means peeling the skin from the head.
rows.anchor: { نزاعة للشوى } يعني: جلود الرأس تقشيرها عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fire calls by name the disbeliever and hypocrite who turned away from faith, and the person who gathered wealth and hoarded it without paying God's due.
rows.anchor: { تدعو } الكافر باسمه والمنافق، فتقول: إلي إلي يا { من أدبر } عن الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity is anxious: hardship makes a person despair, while receiving wealth makes him withhold God's due.
rows.anchor: { إن الإنسان خلق هلوعا } وتفسير الهلوع ما ذكره في قوله: { إذا مسه الشر جزوعا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is believers who are constant in prayer and do not turn away from the prayer direction.
rows.anchor: { الذين هم على صلاتهم دائمون } لا يلتفتون في الصلاة عن سمت القبلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet finds no refuge apart from God.
rows.anchor: { ولن أجد من دونه ملتحدا } أي: ملجأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's role is to convey God's messages; he does not control harm, disbelief, or guidance, as the cited wording says.
rows.anchor: { إلا بلاغا من الله ورسالاته } لكن أبلغ عن الله ما أرسلت به، ولا أملك الكفر والإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When disbelievers see the promised punishment, they will know whether the Prophet or they have the weaker helper and fewer supporters.
rows.anchor: { حتى إذا رأوا } أي: الكفار { ما يوعدون } من العذاب والنار { فسيعلمون } حينئذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet does not know whether the promised punishment is near or whether God will set a distant term for it.
rows.anchor: { قل إن أدري } ما أدري { أقريب ما توعدون } من العذاب { أم يجعل له ربي أمدا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone knows the unseen and reveals it to no one except an approved messenger; angels guard the revelation so devils cannot overhear and pass it to soothsayers claiming prophetic status.
rows.anchor: { عالم الغيب } أي: هو عالم الغيب { فلا يظهر } فلا يطلع على ما غيبه عن العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should leave the polytheist chiefs to God, who will take care of them, and not worry about their affair.
rows.anchor: { وذرني والمكذبين } لا تهتم لشأنهم فإني أكفيكهم، يعني: رؤساء المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage echoes the command to leave God and whoever denies the discourse to Him.
rows.anchor: كقوله: فذرني ومن يكذب بهذا الحديث وقد مر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “People of luxury” are affluent people; they are deferred only until their lifespans end, after which God has shackles and a huge fire.
rows.anchor: { أولي النعمة } ذوي التنعم والترفه { ومهلهم قليلا } يعني: إلى مدة آجالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their choking food cannot pass down the throat and consists of foul fluid, thorny plant, and zaqqūm.
rows.anchor: { وطعاما ذا غصة } يغص في الحلوق ولا يسوغ، وهو الغسلين والضريع والزقوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth and mountains will tremble and move, and mountains will become flowing sand.
rows.anchor: { يوم ترجف الأرض والجبال } تضطرب وتتحرك { وكانت الجبال كثيبا مهيلا } رملا سائلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad was sent as a witness; Pharaoh was seized with a heavy punishment, and disbelievers are asked how they will protect themselves from a day so terrible it turns children gray.
rows.anchor: { إنا أرسلنا إليكم رسولا } محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم { شاهدا عليكم } يشهد عليكم يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “No” rejects the opponents' claim, and the moon begins an oath.
rows.anchor: { كلا } ليس الأمر على ما ذكروا من التكذيب له { والقمر } قسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night “when it recedes” means it comes after the day.
rows.anchor: { والليل إذ أدبر } جاء بعد النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dawn “when it brightens” means it becomes luminous.
rows.anchor: { والصبح إذا أسفر } أضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saqr is one of the great realities, a warning for humanity; people can advance in obedience or fall behind in what is commanded.
rows.anchor: { إنها لإحدى الكبر } إن سقر لإحدى الأمور العظام. { نذيرا } إنذارا { للبشر }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each soul is held by its deeds, except the people of the right, who are people of Paradise and are forgiven their sins.
rows.anchor: { إلا أصحاب اليمين } يعني: أهل الجنة فهم لا يرتهنون بذنوبهم، ولكن الله يغفرها لهم.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies the people of the right as Muslim children.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أصحاب اليمين ها هنا أطفال المسلمين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about when Resurrection comes is asked in denial and dismissal of its occurrence.
rows.anchor: { يسأل أيان } متى { يوم القيامة } تكذيبا به واستبعادا لوقوعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sight is frightened and bewildered, the moon darkens and loses its light, and sun and moon are joined in losing their light.
rows.anchor: { فإذا برق البصر } فزع وتحير.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People ask where to flee, but there is no refuge or shelter; their destination and return is to God.
rows.anchor: { يقول الإنسان يومئذ أين المفر } أي: الفرار؟ { كلا } لا مفر ذلك اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each person is told his earliest and latest deeds; his limbs bear witness, with the feminine form used for emphasis or “the person” referring to the limbs.
rows.anchor: { ينبأ الإنسان } يخبر { بما قدم وأخر } بأول عمله وآخره. { بل الإنسان على نفسه بصيرة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if he argues and offers excuses, his own self disproves them; another interpretation says he cannot hide behind curtains or closed doors, with “maʿādhīr” meaning a curtain in Yemeni speech.
rows.anchor: { ولو ألقى معاذيره } ولو اعتذر وجادل فعليه من نفسه من يكذب عذره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading concerns Adam: forty years passed while he was a clay body, not remembered or known; alternatively, all people were nonexistent before becoming remembered.
rows.anchor: { هل أتى على الإنسان } قد أتى على آدم { حين من الدهر } أربعون سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam's descendants were made from the mixed fluids of man and woman, including their differing colors, to be tested by commands and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: { إنا خلقنا الإنسان } يعني: ابن آدم { من نطفة أمشاج } أخلاط، يعني: ماء الرجل وماء المرأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God clarified the path, making the person grateful or ungrateful; sending messengers made the proof clear whether one believes or disbelieves.
rows.anchor: { إنا هديناه السبيل } بينا له الطريق { إما شاكرا وإما كفورا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People were created in pairs, male and female.
rows.anchor: { وخلقناكم أزواجا } ذكورا وإناثا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sleep rests the body; night clothes everything with darkness, while day provides the means of livelihood.
rows.anchor: { وجعلنا الليل لباسا } يلبس كل شيء بسواده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven firm structures are the well-built heavens, and the blazing hot lamp is the sun.
rows.anchor: { وجعلنا سراجا } أي: الشمس { وهاجا } وقادا حارا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “pressing clouds” are clouds that pour abundant water.
rows.anchor: { وأنزلنا من المعصرات } السحاب { ماء ثجاجا } صبابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain brings out grain for people, plants for livestock, and densely interwoven gardens.
rows.anchor: { لنخرج به حبا } مما يأكله الناس { ونباتا } مما ترعاه النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day of Decision is the appointed time for promised recompense; the raised arrive in groups, the sky opens into gates, and the mountains move like a mirage.
rows.anchor: { إن يوم الفصل كان ميقاتا } لما وعده الله من الجزاء والثواب. { يوم ينفخ في الصور فتأتون أفواجا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge asks whether the deniers or the heavens are greater in creation.
rows.anchor: { أأنتم } أيها المنكرون للبعث { أشد خلقا أم السماء بناها }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God raised the heaven's roof and made it even, without cracks or fissures.
rows.anchor: { رفع سمكها } سقفها { فسواها } بلا شقوق ولا فطور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God darkened the night and brought out its daylight through the sun.
rows.anchor: { وأغطش } أظلم { ليلها وأخرج ضحاها } أظهر نورها بالشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth existed before God spread it out; He brought out water and pasture for livestock.
rows.anchor: { والأرض بعد ذلك دحاها } بسطها، وكانت مخلوقة غير مدحوة. { أخرج منها ماءها ومرعاها }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God set the mountains firmly as a benefit for people and their livestock.
rows.anchor: { والجبال أرساها }. { متاعا } منفعة { لكم ولأنعامكم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Great Overwhelming Event means the blast of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: { فإذا جاءت الطامة الكبرى } يعني: صيحة القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks when the Resurrection will occur and be established.
rows.anchor: { يسألونك عن الساعة } يعني: القيامة. { أيان مرساها } متى وقوعها وثبوتها؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad has no knowledge of its time; knowledge of its final limit belongs to God.
rows.anchor: { فيم أنت } يا محمد { من ذكراها } أي: ليس عندك علمها. { إلى ربك منتهاها }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's warning benefits those who fear the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: { إنما أنت منذر من يخشاها } إنما ينفع إنذارك من يخشاها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At its sight, people will think they spent only an evening or morning in their graves, underestimating the time because of the terror they see.
rows.anchor: { كأنهم يوم يرونها لم يلبثوا } في قبورهم { إلا عشية أو ضحاها } أي: نهارها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dense gardens, fruit, and pasture are provisions for people and livestock.
rows.anchor: { وحدائق غلبا } بساتين كثيرة الأشجار. { وفاكهة وأبا } أي: الكلأ الذي ترعاه الماشية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deafening cry is the cry of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: { فإذا جاءت الصاخة } صيحة القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person flees his brother, parents, spouse, and children, paying attention to none because he is occupied with himself.
rows.anchor: { يوم يفر المرء من أخيه }. { وأمه وأبيه }. { وصاحبته وبنيه } لا يلتفت إلى واحد منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every person is so occupied with his own affair that he cannot attend to another's.
rows.anchor: { لكل امرىء منهم يومئذ شأن يغنيه } يشغله عن شأن غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some faces will be bright, laughing and rejoicing.
rows.anchor: { وجوه يومئذ مسفرة } مضيئة. { ضاحكة مستبشرة } فرحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other faces will be dusty and covered by dark gloom; they are the disbelieving sinners.
rows.anchor: { ووجوه يومئذ عليها غبرة } غبار. { ترهقها } تغشاها { قترة } ظلمة وسواد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the neighboring oath, one view says night “when it darkens” means its arrival; another says its departure.
rows.anchor: { والليل إذا عسعس } أقبل بظلامه، وقيل: أدبر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dawn's breathing means its light extends until it becomes clear day.
rows.anchor: { والصبح إذا تنفس } امتد حتى يصير نهارا بينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an was brought down by Gabriel, who is strong and has rank with the Lord of the Throne.
rows.anchor: { ذي قوة } من صفة جبريل { عند ذي العرش مكين } ذي مكانة ومنزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People labor for their Lord and ultimately meet their deeds at Resurrection.
rows.anchor: { يا أيها الإنسان إنك كادح إلى ربك كدحا } عامل لربك عملا { فملاقيه } فملاق عملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person given the record in his right hand receives an easy account, meaning a presentation of the record, since close questioning brings punishment; he returns joyfully to his family in Paradise.
rows.anchor: { فسوف يحاسب حسابا يسيرا } وهو العرض على الله عز وجل؛ لأن من نوقش الحساب عذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With his hands chained to his neck, the other person receives the record in his left hand from behind, calls destruction on himself, and enters the Fire.
rows.anchor: { وأما من أوتي كتابه وراء ظهره } وذلك أن يديه غلتا إلى عنقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He enjoyed himself among his family and followed his desires, assuming he would never return to God; contrary to his thought, he will return.
rows.anchor: { إنه كان في أهله } في الدنيا { مسرورا } متابعا لهواه. { إنه ظن أن لن يحور }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The negating particle means “I swear”; the twilight is the red after sunset.
rows.anchor: { فلا أقسم } معناه فأقسم { بالشفق } وهو الحمرة التي ترى بعد سقوط الشمس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies the twilight oath with night and day.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يعني: الليل والنهار.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath by dawn means every day's dawn.
rows.anchor: { والفجر } يعني: فجر كل يوم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ten nights are the ten days of Dhū al-Ḥijja.
rows.anchor: { وليال عشر } عشر ذي الحجة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The even is the Day of Sacrifice, day ten; the odd is ʿArafa, day nine.
rows.anchor: { والشفع } يعني: يوم النحر؛ لأنه يوم العاشر { والوتر } يوم عرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passing night is the night at Muzdalifa as it leaves; another view says when it arrives.
rows.anchor: { والليل إذا يسر } يعني: ليل المزدلفة إذا مضى وذهب. وقيل: إذا جاء وأقبل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath suffices as a compelling argument for a person of reason.
rows.anchor: { هل في ذلك } الذي ذكرت { قسم لذي حجر } أي: مقنع ومكتفى في القسم لذي عقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They neither urge one another to feed the poor nor help with it.
rows.anchor: { ولا تحاضون على طعام المسكين } لا تأمرون به، ولا تعينون عليه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They voraciously consume orphans' inheritances, withholding the orphan's share, and love wealth greatly.
rows.anchor: { وتأكلون التراث } يعني: ميراث اليتامى { أكلا لما } شديدا، تجمعون المال كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth shakes and breaks itself apart; God's command and judgment arrive with angels standing in rows.
rows.anchor: { إذا دكت الأرض دكا دكا } إذا زلزلت الأرض فكسر بعضها بعضا. { وجاء ربك } أي: أمر ربك وقضاؤه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell is brought on seventy thousand reins, each held by seventy thousand angels; the disbeliever manifests repentance, but it is too late.
rows.anchor: { وجيء يومئذ بجهنم } تقاد بسبعين ألف زمام، كل زمام بأيدي سبعين ألف ملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person longs to have sent deeds ahead for the afterlife, where there is no death.
rows.anchor: { يقول يا ليتني قدمت لحياتي } أي: للدار الآخرة التي لا موت فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one carries out God's punishment in His place; the command belongs to Him alone that Day.
rows.anchor: { فيومئذ لا يعذب عذابه أحد } لا يتولى عذاب الله تعالى يومئذ أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The negating particle affirms and reinforces “I swear”; the city is Mecca.
rows.anchor: { لا أقسم } المعنى: أقسم، و { لا } توكيد. { بهذا البلد } يعني: مكة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet was permitted to do as he wished in Mecca, including killing and taking captives, for an hour on the day of its conquest.
rows.anchor: { وأنت } يا محمد { حل بهذا البلد } تصنع فيه ما تريد من القتل والأسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The father is Adam and his offspring are what he begot; “mā” means “who.”
rows.anchor: { ووالد } أقسم بآدم عليه السلام { وما ولد } وولده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human life is hardship in worldly and afterlife affairs; another view reads the phrase as upright in stature.
rows.anchor: { لقد خلقنا الإنسان في كبد } أي: مشقة يكابد أمر الدنيا والآخرة وشدائدهما. وقيل منتصبا معتدلا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed about the strong man Abū al-Ashaddayn of Banū Jumah, who assumed no one could overpower him, though God can.
rows.anchor: { أيحسب أن لن يقدر عليه أحد } نزلت في رجل من بني جمح يكنى أبا الأشدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man falsely boasts that he spent much wealth in opposition to Muhammad.
rows.anchor: { يقول أهلكت مالا } على عداوة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم { لبدا } كثيرا بعضه على بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God saw his spending and knows its amount.
rows.anchor: { أيحسب أن لم يره أحد } في إنفاقه، فيعلم مقدار نفقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eyes, tongue, lips, and the two paths signify that God can create and account for what a person does; the two paths mean good and evil.
rows.anchor: { ألم نجعل له عينين }. { ولسانا وشفتين }. { وهديناه النجدين } يقول: ألم نعرفه طريق الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The difficult ascent is a metaphor for the costly effort of spending in God's obedience; this person did not spend in obedience, and freeing a slave means paying for its emancipation.
rows.anchor: { فلا اقتحم العقبة } أي: لم يدخل العقبة، وهذا مثل ضربه الله تعالى للمنفق في طاعة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A day of severe hunger is a famine.
rows.anchor: { أو إطعام في يوم ذي مسغبة } مجاعة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An orphan “of close relationship” is a relative.
rows.anchor: { يتيما ذا مقربة } ذا قرابة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poor person “of dust” is so impoverished he is stuck to the soil.
rows.anchor: { أو مسكينا ذا متربة } أي: ذا فقر قد لصق من فقره بالتراب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Freeing a slave and feeding only count as crossing the ascent when the person also believes; believers counsel one another to obey God patiently and show mercy to creation.
rows.anchor: { ثم كان من الذين آمنوا } أي: كان مقتحم العقبة وفاك الرقبة والمطعم من الذين آمنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those with these qualities are among the people of the right; the people of the left are disbelievers, or the fortunate and unfortunate in relation to themselves, and Hell is sealed over them.
rows.anchor: { أولئك أصحاب الميمنة } من كان بهذه الصفة فهو من جملة أصحاب اليمين. { والذين كفروا بآياتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun's “morning brightness” means its light.
rows.anchor: { والشمس وضحاها } وضيائها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: During the first half of the month the moon follows the sun in light and replaces it.
rows.anchor: { والقمر إذا تلاها } تبعها في الضياء والنور، وذلك في النصف الأول من الشهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Day uncovers darkness; another view says it reveals and shows the sun as the day spreads.
rows.anchor: { والنهار إذا جلاها } جلى الظلمة وكشفها. وقيل: جلى الشمس وبينها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night covers the sun.
rows.anchor: { والليل إذا يغشاها } يستر الشمس.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other oaths concern the construction of the sky, the spreading of earth, and the formation of the soul.
rows.anchor: { والسماء وما بناها } أي: وبنائها. { والأرض وما طحاها } وطحوها، أي: بسطها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God taught the soul obedience and disobedience.
rows.anchor: { فألهمها فجورها وتقواها } علمها الطاعة والمعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The daylight appears and becomes manifest.
rows.anchor: { والنهار إذا تجلى } بان وظهر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the creator of male and female, and the oath's answer is that people's deeds differ, especially those of believer and disbeliever; the passage was revealed about Abū Bakr and Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥarb.
rows.anchor: { وما خلق } ومن خلق { الذكر والأنثى } وهو الله تعالى، [وجواب القسم وهو قوله:] { إن سعيكم لشتى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The giver spends wealth, fears his Lord, and avoids His prohibitions.
rows.anchor: { فأما من أعطى } ماله { واتقى } ربه واجتنب محارمه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The best” means certainty God will repay him; another view reads it as belief in God's oneness.
rows.anchor: { وصدق بالحسنى } أيقن بأن الله سبحانه سيخلف عليه. وقيل: صدق ب لا إله إلا الله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God prepares the easy course of deeds pleasing to Him; Abū Bakr exemplified it by buying and freeing people tortured to make them renounce Islam, in confidence of God's reward.
rows.anchor: { فسنيسره } فسنهيئه { لليسرى } للخلة اليسرى، أي: الأمر السهل من العمل بما يرضي الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The miser withholds spending for good and considers himself independent of God, without hoping for His reward.
rows.anchor: { وأما من بخل } بالنفقة في الخير { واستغنى } عن الله، فلم يرغب في ثوابه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God abandons him to works that lead to punishment and a difficult end.
rows.anchor: { فسنيسره للعسرى } أي: نخذله حتى يعمل بما يؤديه إلى العذاب والأمر العسير.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wealth cannot benefit a person when he dies and perishes; another interpretation says when he falls into Hell.
rows.anchor: { وما يغني عنه ماله إذا تردى } أي: مات وهلك. وقيل: سقط في جهنم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God undertakes to clarify guidance and error and owns both afterlife and worldly life; seeking them from another is a mistake.
rows.anchor: { إن علينا للهدى } أي: إن علينا أن نبين طريق الهدى من طريق الضلال. { وإن لنا للآخرة والأولى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning is of a blazing fire that only the disbeliever who denied and turned away enters.
rows.anchor: { فأنذرتكم } خوفتكم { نارا تلظى } تتوقد. { لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى } لا يدخلها إلا الكافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most God-fearing, identified as Abū Bakr, is kept from the Fire and gives wealth to seek purification with God, not fame or show.
rows.anchor: { وسيجنبها } أي: يبعد منها { الأتقى } يعني: أبا بكر رضوان الله عليه. { الذي يؤتي ماله يتزكى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When disbelievers claimed Abū Bakr freed Bilāl to repay an old favor, God clarified that he owed nobody a favor in return.
rows.anchor: { وما لأحد عنده من نعمة تجزى } وذلك أن الكفار قالوا لما اشترى أبو بكر رضي الله عنه بلالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forenoon means the whole day; night has settled with its darkness.
rows.anchor: { والضحى } أي: النهار كله. { والليل إذا سجى } سكن بالخلق واستقر بظلامه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God did not leave or hate Muhammad after choosing and loving him; this is the answer to the oath. Revelation had paused for fifteen days, prompting people to say God abandoned and hated him, so the surah was revealed.
rows.anchor: { ما ودعك ربك وما قلى } وما تركك منذ اختارك، وما أبغضك منذ أحبك، وهذا جواب القسم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife is better for Muhammad because of its honors and ranks, and God will give him reward and intercession until he is satisfied.
rows.anchor: { وللآخرة خير لك من الأولى } لأن الله يعطيك فيها الكرامات والدرجات. { ولسوف يعطيك ربك }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet vowed not to be satisfied while one member of his community remained in the Fire.
rows.anchor: يروى أنه قال عليه السلام لما نزلت هذه الآية: إذن لا أرضى وواحد من أمتي في النار.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical question asserts God opened, expanded, and softened Muhammad's heart with faith, prophethood, knowledge, and wisdom.
rows.anchor: { ألم نشرح لك صدرك } ألم نفتح ونوسع، ونلين لك قلبك بالإيمان والنبوة، والعلم والحكمة؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The removed burden may mean past pre-Islamic faults, mistakes and forgetfulness, or the heavy responsibilities of prophethood; linguistically, a burden is a weighty load pressing on the back.
rows.anchor: { ووضعنا } [حططنا] { عنك وزرك } ما سلف منك في الجاهلية. وقيل: يعني: الخطأ والسهو.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God raised Muhammad's mention so that he is mentioned whenever God is mentioned.
rows.anchor: { ورفعنا لك ذكرك } أي: إذا ذكرت ذكرت معي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ease with the current hardship means God will make Muhammad prevail over the polytheists until they submit willingly or unwillingly.
rows.anchor: { فإن مع العسر يسرا } أي: مع الشدة التي أنت فيها من مقاساة بلاء المشركين يسرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repetition emphasizes assurance; another reading generalizes the promise to every hardship, with ease in this life or the next, and says one hardship has two eases.
rows.anchor: { إن مع العسر يسرا } تكرار للتأكيد. وقيل: إن هذا عام في كل عسر أصاب المؤمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fig and olive are two mountains in Syria named Mount Tīn and Mount Zaytā in Syriac because those trees grow there; Sinai is Moses' mountain and “Sinīn” means blessed in Syriac.
rows.anchor: { والتين والزيتون } هما جبلان بالشام، طور تينا، وطور زيتا بالسريانية، سميا بالتين والزيتون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The secure city is Mecca, called secure because its people are not attacked.
rows.anchor: { وهذا البلد الأمين } [الآمن]. يعني: مكة، سماه أمينا لأنه آمن لا يهاج أهله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best form is a balanced upright figure that can take food by hand.
rows.anchor: { لقد خلقنا الإنسان في أحسن تقويم } صورة؛ لأنه معتدل القامة، يتناول مأكوله بيده.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation takes the lowest of the low to mean extreme old age, when people become elderly, chronically ill, or weak.
rows.anchor: { ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين } إلى أرذل العمر، والسافلون: هم الهرمى والزمنى والضعفى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī prefers the interpretation that disbelievers are returned to Hell; a believer in extreme old age retains the reward of former deeds, and “unfailing” means uncut off.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معنى: { ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين }: إلى النار، يعني: الكافر، ثم استثنى المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Calamity is so named because its terrors strike hearts; the repeated question magnifies and terrifies, as with al-Ḥāqqa.
rows.anchor: { القارعة } يعني: القارعة؛ لأنها تقرع القلوب بأهوالها. { ما القارعة } تفخيم لشأنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People at resurrection move confusedly among each other like a scattered mass of locusts, and mountains become light, carded wool.
rows.anchor: { يوم يكون الناس كالفراش } كغوغاء الجراد لا يتجه إلى جهة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scales made heavy with good deeds lead to a life one is pleased with.
rows.anchor: { فأما من ثقلت موازينه } بالحسنات. { فهو في عيشة راضية } يرضاها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person whose scales are light has the Fire as his home, explained as intensely hot.
rows.anchor: { وأما من خفت موازينه }. { فأمه هاوية } فمسكنه النار. { وما أدراك ماهيه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Competition in wealth, children, and numbers distracted people from obedience until death; the passage was revealed about Jews who boasted that their groups and descendants outnumbered one another, then died in error.
rows.anchor: { ألهاكم التكاثر }. { حتى زرتم المقابر } شغلكم التكاثر بالأموال والأولاد والعدد عن طاعة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At death, they will know the evil consequence of their conduct.
rows.anchor: { كلا } ليس الأمر الذي ينبغي أن تكونوا عليه التكاثر { سوف تعلمون } عند النزع سوء عاقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the grave they will again know the consequence; repetition reinforces the threat.
rows.anchor: { ثم كلا سوف تعلمون } سوء عاقبة ما كنتم عليه في القبر، والتكرير لتأكيد التهديد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Certain knowledge would distract them from their present rivalry; the conditional's answer is omitted, then the text says they will see Hell plainly with the eye of certainty.
rows.anchor: { كلا لو تعلمون علم اليقين } أي: لو علمتم الأمر حق علمه لشغلكم ذلك عما أنتم فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿAṣr means time, by which God swears.
rows.anchor: { والعصر } هو الدهر، أقسم الله به.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person in loss is the disbeliever who works outside obedience and forfeits family, place, and home in Paradise.
rows.anchor: { إن الإنسان } يعني: الكافر العامل لغير طاعة الله { لفي خسر } خسران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers escape loss through faith, good works, mutual counsel to remain firm in monotheism and faith, and patience in obedience and striving in God's path.
rows.anchor: { وتواصوا بالحق } وصى بعضهم بالإقامة على التوحيد والإيمان { وتواصوا بالصبر }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet maps the passages onto Abū Jahl, Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, and ʿAlī respectively.
rows.anchor: ويروى [مرفوعا]: { إن الإنسان لفي خسر } يعني: أبا جهل، { إلا الذين آمنوا } يعني: أبا بكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage is reported to concern al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil; another report names al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, and another names Abū Sufyān, who struck an orphan asking him for food after slaughtering a camel. “Repelling the orphan” means harshly pushing him from his due.
rows.anchor: { أرأيت الذي يكذب بالدين } نزلت في العاص بن وائل. وقيل: نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He neither feeds the poor nor urges others to feed them.
rows.anchor: { ولا يحض على طعام المسكين } لا يطعم المسكين ولا يأمر بإطعامه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heedless prayer-goers delay prayer beyond its appointed time.
rows.anchor: { الذين هم عن صلاتهم ساهون } غافلون يؤخرونها عن وقتها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Show-offs are hypocrites who pray publicly and abandon prayer in private.
rows.anchor: { الذين هم يراؤون } يعني: المنافقين يصلون في العلانية، ويتركون الصلاة في السر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The withheld aid includes zakat and useful items such as an axe, pot, water, or salt.
rows.anchor: { ويمنعون الماعون } الزكاة وما فيه منفعة من الفأس والقدر والماء والملح.
